comments.body: Operator context (2026-08-14), recorded so this work is interpreted correctly: the verifier was originally a simple harness-native read-only subagent and was reliable; runaway tool calls / context overruns appeared only after the harness-independent transition, and the banking/budget/recovery machinery is containment for those emergent failure modes. This ticket (generous budgets + child-traversal term + PASS-verdict cache) is INTERIM SYMPTOM RELIEF and proceeds as planned — but it is not a direction to extend. The long-term direction is viral-peppy-lowchen (b4be-0ed8-22cb-4b01): deterministic evidence prepack + single-pass verdict, demoting banking/budget to a rarely-exercised runaway backstop. Any further verifier complexity must justify itself against that simple-core goal.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PS3 pushed (change 1796): closed a correctness seam operator review found in PS2's verdict cache.

The seam: scoped_content_fingerprint resolved blobs at hard-literal HEAD:<path> (health probe HEAD^{tree}). But a --ref <sha>-targeted close (bug 80af, stacked-story flow: transition_close.py resolves the SAME ref for drift checks and threads ref into the completion precheck/verify) verifies and signs against THAT ref's tree — so verdicts proven against the story's tree would have been persisted under a fingerprint of the TIP's blobs: the cache would assert "these blobs <-> PASS" for blobs the verifier never examined, and a later re-verify at a matching-tip HEAD could seed those verdicts illegitimately.

How the ref reaches the verify flow: verify_completion (completion.py) resolves the gate handle via gate_source.resolve_gate_handle(ref, ...) whose SnapshotHandle.sha is the pinned resolved commit (annotate_result stamps it as verified_at_sha). PS3 threads handle.sha as a new verify_ref kwarg: verify_completion -> _verify_completion_inner -> gate_dispatch.produce_completion_verdict -> CompletionAgentStep(verify_ref=...) -> the cache calls.

Cache surface changes (completion_verdict_cache.py): scoped_content_fingerprint/load_valid_pass_entries/seed_bank_from_cache/persist_pass_verdicts gain kw-only ref=None (None -> "HEAD", byte-compatible default); specs become <ref>:<path> and <ref>^{tree} — the rev-parse subcommand stays literal so the raw-git gate stays green. Persist fingerprints at the ref the verdicts were proven against; load/seed fingerprint at the CURRENT run's verification target. Each entry additionally records verified_ref_sha (resolved commit sha) — informational audit stamp only, never a validity key (keying on it would kill reuse across unrelated commits).

Tests (RED-first, all in test_completion_verdict_cache.py, now 21 tests): test_persist_under_ref_binds_the_refs_blobs_not_heads (impact file differs between ref and HEAD -> entry fingerprint matches recompute at ref, not HEAD; verified_ref_sha == ref sha), test_ref_bound_entry_does_not_seed_at_a_differing_head (no load/seed at HEAD; loads AND seeds at the matching ref), test_default_ref_is_head_byte_compatible.

Mutation pass on the ref logic: 5 mutants (fingerprint ignores ref; persist drops ref pass-through; load's fingerprint drops ref; verified_ref_sha resolved at HEAD; seed drops ref pass-through) — 5/5 killed (the seed pass-through mutant initially survived; killed by extending the seeding assertions).

Gates: check_raw_git_writes rc=0, make lint clean (complexity ratchet new=0/increased=0), make typecheck clean (543 files), targeted suites 86/86 (cache 21, banking, budget contracts, review-output-budget). Module caps respected: completion.py 800, completion_recovery.py 799 (comment trims offset the threading lines).

compiled_state.description:
## Problem
The verifier's step budget routinely exhausts on legitimate validation, failing criteria as "unmet" that are merely unproven-within-budget (fb8a: request_limit=24, 2 false unmets; pony: repeated exhaustion, 5 then 1 false unmets). The pressure drives operators toward attestation-laundering.

## Design intent (operator-stated)
The budget's ONLY goal is preventing runaway tool use. For valid tool use the floor must be GENEROUS with ample scaling; we never artificially limit authorized validation.

## Current mechanics
`verify_step_floor(c) = clamp(steps_per_criterion x c, step_floor_min, 480)`, defaults 8/48; structured_run halves steps into request_limit (6-AC epic: 48 steps = 24 requests). Defects: (1) story-calibrated cost model — epic criteria traverse child tickets (show_ticket + comments + repo reads, 5-10 requests each) plus fixed overhead, no evidence-surface term; (2) runaway is ALREADY separately guarded (tool_calls_limit, loop detection, the clamp), so a small budget adds no safety, only false FAILs; (3) no cross-run carryover — every re-verify re-proves all criteria (~10 min/cycle).

## Plan
1. Raise defaults: completion_verify_steps_per_criterion 8 -> 24, completion_verify_step_floor_min 48 -> 160 (supersedes the interim operator-machine config mitigation). Raise the 480 clamp to 960 so 24/criterion scales past 20 ACs — the clamp is a runaway ceiling, not a validation cap.
2. Evidence-surface scaling: budget = per_criterion x c + child_traversal x direct_children + fixed_overhead, with defaults child_traversal = 16 steps/direct child and fixed_overhead = 16 steps (mid-band of observed 5-10 requests/child at the 2x steps halving; initial show_ticket+parse sizes the same). Both are new config keys: typed VerifyConfig fields (defaults 16) in _config_schema.py (:249-250 area) AND validators in _config_sections.py:35-36 style. Children counted from the ticket graph at budget-sizing time; any enumeration/read error at the completion.py:780 site fails OPEN to direct_children=0, preserving its "enumeration must not raise" invariant (criteria_count already fail-closes to 0 there, keeping the lean-install typed missing-extra LLMError path). The child term lands INSIDE `verify_step_floor` (new `direct_children: int = 0` param), NOT at the sizing call — its exactly-two consumers, primary sizing (completion.py:780) and `plan_recovery_pool` (completion_banking.py:224), stay on one formula. `plan_recovery_pool` gains a pass-through `direct_children` param (default 0) forwarded by its sole caller (completion_recovery.py:625); its docstring oracle pins (c=8 -> floor 64, N 32, global 48, successor 16; clamp-max) update to 24/160/960 mechanics with childless + childful rows.
3. Cross-run PASS-verdict cache — a NEW ticket-scoped store; the run-scoped `CriterionBank` (completion_banking.py:396-435) stays as designed (run-unique dir = concurrent-close isolation). Cache at `.rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/<ticket>/<criterion-hash>.json`, written ONLY on a validated PASS at finalize (atomic tmp+rename; last-write-wins safe). Invalidation: NOT the whole-repo HEAD tree sha (`_resolve_tree_sha` :358-373 — any unrelated commit rotates it); key each entry by (criterion-text hash, scoped content fingerprint).The scoped fingerprint is NET-NEW code (BankStamps' material_fingerprint hashes PLAN TEXT, not file bytes): a new helper resolves each file_impact path to its git BLOB SHA (batch `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`) and hashes the sorted (path, blob-sha) pairs; absent path -> sentinel; git failure disables reuse for the run (fail-open to re-verification); when own file_impact is empty but the ticket has children (the epic case), the fingerprint unions direct-child file_impact blobs (DIRECT children from the ticket graph, the same list budget sizing uses) — NOT `_subtree_impacts` (completion_prefetch.py:257; whole-subtree BFS, {path:count} frequencies not blobs, excludes root). Whole-tree sha is the fallback ONLY for childless tickets with empty file_impact. Cache entries store the FULL banked record (met, evidence, citations); at run start (completion_recovery.py:487 `CriterionBank.for_run`) still-valid entries are SEEDED into the run's bank, stamped `seeded: true`. Seeded ids are EXCLUDED from the primary's work surface twice over: (a) `primary_criteria_manifest` (DEFINED completion_banking.py:193, signature (expected, id_by_text); recovery.py:540 is its call site in `_primary_manifest_contract`) gains a `seeded_ids` frozenset param threaded through _primary_manifest_contract and omits those ids; (b) since the manifest is data-only, the primary context ALSO annotates each seeded criterion's prose with an "already credited — do not re-verify" directive, so the primary (launched first, :495) actually skips them. Finalizer interaction: `merge_finalizer_with_bank` today PRESERVES the finalizer's met on echoed records (only the evidence_sufficient marker re-stamps via `_restamp_marker`), so this plan SCOPES A CHANGE: `seeded: true` records bypass finalizer judgment — an echo (incl. a met:false downgrade) is replaced by the bank's validated-PASS record, an omission appended from the bank. Same-run (non-seeded) downgrade preservation unchanged — the rule keys strictly on the seeded flag. RED test: an echo that drops OR downgrades a seeded criterion still yields the credited verdict; a same-run downgrade is still preserved. Exhaustion converges across runs. (Marker semantics from 1d71-a76c: cached entries are PASS-only; insufficiency never cached.)
4. Runaway guards stay authoritative: tool_calls_limit + loop detection unchanged; document at verify_step_floor that the budget exists ONLY for runaway prevention.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Defaults raised (24/160; clamp 960), rationale documented at verify_step_floor; a 6-AC epic sizes to >=80 requests, a 15-AC epic to >=180; formula unit tests, INCLUDING updating the hard-coded pins in tests/interfaces/contracts/test_completion_budget.py (verify_step_floor(1)==48, (8)==64, (40)==320, (100)==480, captured max_iterations==48, _VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX==480) to the new mechanics.
- [x] Budget sizing adds a child-traversal term inside verify_step_floor (new direct_children param, default 0) so BOTH consumers — completion.py:780 primary sizing and plan_recovery_pool (completion_banking.py:224, forwarded by completion_recovery.py:625) — share the formula; new VerifyConfig fields + _config_sections validators for the two keys; epic-fixture test (childful sizes strictly larger than childless at equal criteria count, primary AND recovery pool; enumeration failure -> direct_children=0, no raise); plan_recovery_pool docstring pins AND the hard-coded pins in tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_banking.py:53-67 (floor/N/global/successor) updated to the new mechanics plus a childful row.
- [x] A re-verify after exhaustion credits still-valid cached PASS verdicts (same scoped fingerprint + criterion text) by seeding them into the run-scoped CriterionBank with the seeded flag; the primary manifest omits seeded ids AND the primary context marks each seeded criterion "already credited — do not re-verify" (both tested); the merge path credits seeded records verbatim (finalizer echo/omission cannot downgrade them) while same-run finalizer downgrades stay preserved; invalidation RED->GREEN on fingerprint or text change, INCLUDING an in-scope content edit (a file under file_impact changes, ticket text unchanged -> blob sha rotates -> cached PASS invalidated); an unrelated commit outside file_impact does NOT invalidate; run-scoped bank concurrent-close isolation regression-tested.
- [x] Runaway protection regression-guarded: tool_calls_limit and loop detection unchanged; a looping-tool fixture still trips the backstop under the larger budget.
(trimmed for admission cap)
compiled_state.title: Completion-verifier budget: generous runaway-only floor, evidence-surface scaling, cross-run bank persistence
